chunks: He heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
'The owner of wealth is more rightful with (the disposition of) his wealth for as long as there remains something of the soul within him — he may place it wherever he wishes.'

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: more rightful/entitled — a comparative form in Arabic indicating priority of claim
key_terms.الرُّوحِ: the soul/spirit — here used as a metaphor for life itself; as long as there is 'something of the soul' means 'as long as one is alive'
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْمَالِ: owner of wealth — the person who holds legal title to property

ai.seo_question: Does a dying person retain control over their wealth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a person retains full legal authority over their own wealth throughout their lifetime, so long as life remains in them. This hadith is narrated by 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati and provides the foundational Shia jurisprudential principle that a dying person's testamentary dispositions and gifts have legal force — the owner's agency over their property persists until death. In the context of Islamic inheritance law debates, this ruling affirmed the right to make wills and dispose of wealth freely, countering any claim that incapacitation or illness could limit such authority.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Abu Al Hassan Al Sabaty, from Ammar Bin Musa, who heard
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘The owner of the wealth is more rightful with (the distribution of) his wealth so long as there is something within him from the soul. He can place it wherever he so wishes to’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from abu al-Hassan al-Sabady from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying,
‘The owner of the asset has a greater degree of rights in his assets as long as there is some spirit in him. He can do about it whatever he wants.”’
